idiom_name: private-property composition + use{} over AutoCloseable, interface delegation with by
implementation_notes: A Kotlin whole is a class whose private properties are its parts; composition is language-level, and `by` delegation lets the whole publish a part's interface as its own (the Whole presents one interface) with no hand-written forwarding. kotlin.io.use wraps an AutoCloseable (java.io.Closeable included): it closes the receiver even when the block throws, folds a closing failure into the original exception's suppressed list, and returns the block's value - that is the idiomatic release path for a whole that owns a resource, with the whole's close() cascading to its parts. The JVM has no destructors, so an unclosed whole leaks its non-memory parts and Cleaner-style APIs only backstop missed close() calls. The classic Whole/Part classes stay unnecessary until parts are created or replaced at runtime.
pitfalls: JVM destruction is GC-driven: skipping use{} (or returning out of the wrong scope) leaves file handles and connections open indefinitely; close() must also be idempotent.
A `by`-delegated interface is stored in a private field but its lifetime is not managed: the whole must still close the delegate, and overriding a delegated member silently stops the forwarding.
Registering `this` in a listener or Cleaner action from inside the whole prevents collection or leaks the whole - register a state object that does not capture it.
